records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: CoNiCrFeMn High Entropy Alloy (HEA) nanowire. Intervention: Temperature lowered from 300 K to 77 K. Processing: Molecular dynamics simulation with constant strain rate of 10^8 1/s. Test conditions: Tensile deformation at 77 K. Structure change: Dominant deformation mechanism shifted to twinning induced plasticity (TWIP) with limited FCC-HCP martensitic transformation; partial re-orientation from (110) to (100) phase occurred. Property change: Exceptional strength-ductility trade-off; peak stress reached ~6.2 GPa at 5-6% elongation; delayed necking resulting in high elongation to fracture. Mechanism: Simultaneous activation of twinning induced plasticity and transformation induced plasticity; lattice distortion hinders partial dislocation motion. Evidence: simulated. Quote: "In HEA NWs, dominant deformation mechanism is TWIP, aided by limited FCC-HCP martensitic transformation during the structural re-orientation"
